 Major fried chicken chain franchisee files Chapter 11 bankruptcy
 Kirk O’Neil Tue, November 17, 2026 at 8:17 AM PST 4 min read Although consumer traffic at fried chicken restaurants increased by 3% in 2025, according to data firm  Circana , certain major franchisees have continued to struggle with declining sales and rising costs. 
 Declining sales led a KFC and Taco Bell franchisee to file for bankruptcy to seek a sale of its assets. 
 KFC and Taco Bell restaurant franchisee Tasty Chick'n files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy seeking to sell its assets.Bloomberg / Getty Images Tasty Chick'n files Chapter 11 bankruptcy 
 Major KFC and KFC/Taco Bell co-branded franchisee Tasty Chick'n LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, facing a potential termination of its franchise agreements over $15.6 million in unpaid royalties. 
 The Plano, Texas-based fried chicken dining chain franchisee and three affiliates filed their petition in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas, listing $50 million to $100 million in assets and $100 million to $500 million in liabilities, according to court papers. 
 Read more: Major burger chain buying 163 franchisee units out of bankruptcy 
 Debtor counsel Jason S. Brookner of Gray Reed in Houston was not immediately available for comment. 
 Tasty Chick'n was formed in 2021 to develop, acquire, own, and operate KFC and Taco Bell branded restaurants through franchise agreements with KFC, Taco Bell, and parent Yum Brands, according to a declaration by Tasty Chick'n CEO Thomas M. Scott . 
 Debtor seeks a sale of its assets 
 The franchisee is seeking a sale of its assets through the Chapter 11 bankruptcy case, the declaration said. It plans to market its restaurants as an entire portfolio, by individual market, or in combinations of different markets to maximize buyer participation and transaction value, court papers said. 
 The debtor will also seek $20 million in debtor-in-possession financing from prepetition lender MidCap Financial Trust, consisting of $5 million in new money and a $15 million rollup of prepetition debt.

 The debtor owns and operates 75 KFC and 9 KFC/Taco Bell co-branded restaurants in 10 states, including Florida, Tennessee, Arkansas, Missouri, Mississippi, Alabama, Virginia, Kentucky, Illinois, and Indiana. 
 The fried chicken and taco fast-food franchisee asserted that revenue had declined significantly since the debtors acquired its restaurants, while food, labor, operating, and rent costs all increased, resulting in deteriorating restaurant-level EBITDA. 
 Yum Brands sends default notice 
 Story Continues Tasty Chick'n's franchise agreements impose substantial remodel and upgrade obligations, which have led to $15.6 million in unpaid royalties. Yum Brands sent the debtors a notice of breaches and defaults on Dec. 17, 2025, under the relationship agreement, franchise agreements, and franchise guaranties, court papers said. 
 The debtor sought a forbearance arrangement with Yum Brands but could not reach an agreement. The franchisor sent Tasty Chick'n a notice of intent to terminate its agreements on Sept. 15, 2026, and sought to address the debtor's liquidity and business issues to achieve either a consensual out-of-court restructuring or Chapter 11 process. 
 Termination of the franchise agreements would end the debtor's right to operate the restaurants under the KFC and Taco Bell brands, trigger an event of default under its credit agreement, and eliminate the going-concern value of the company, according to the declaration. 
 3 years of declining sales 
 Tasty Chick'n reported declining sales over the last three years, falling by 11.4% in fiscal year 2024, then 1.4% in fiscal year 2025, and 2.8% so far in 2026. As sales declined, costs continued rising with restaurant margins declining from 11.8% in fiscal 2023 to 4% so far in fiscal 2026. 
 The franchisee's declining sales follow the broader KFC chain's declining sales in the U.S., which fell 6% in the third quarter of 2026, according to the declaration. 
 Tasty Chick'n's largest unsecured creditors include Tasty Restaurant Group LLC, owed over $5 million; McLane Foodservice Inc., owed over $927,000; Brink's Capital LLC, owed over $523,000; NNN REIT, owed over $470,000; and One System Pop, owed over $382,000.
